requirements.requirement: Run Redis across node1, node2, and node3, initially with node1 primary and node2/node3 synchronized replicas.
requirements.summary: Authenticated ROLE and replication checks before disruption showed node1 as primary with two connected replicas; node2 and node3 were synchronized replicas linked to node1. Final checks showed all services active and enabled.

requirements.requirement: Operate three Sentinels monitoring the Redis service as infra-primary.
requirements.summary: Each Sentinel identified infra-primary, two replicas, two peer Sentinels, and three usable Sentinels with quorum and failover authorization available.

requirements.requirement: Provide authenticated TLS for Redis on 6379 and Sentinel on 26379 over the cache network.
requirements.summary: On every cache-network address, authenticated mutual-TLS connections returned PONG for both services. Plaintext, certificate-less, and unauthenticated probes were rejected; Redis reported its plaintext port disabled, TLS port 6379 enabled, and client certificates required. Certificates validated and contained the corresponding cache IP SAN.

requirements.requirement: Place usable administrative credentials in /root/redis-admin.env on node1.
requirements.summary: The file was nonempty, root-owned with mode 0600, contained nonempty authentication variables and Redis/Sentinel connection and TLS paths, and referenced readable credential material.

requirements.requirement: Store infra:proof=ready and retain it across replication and recovery.
requirements.summary: The initial SET succeeded and WAIT received acknowledgements from both replicas. The value remained ready on all nodes after failover and the sequential node reboots.

requirements.requirement: Automatically promote a replica when node1 is unavailable, then return node1 as a synchronized replica.
requirements.summary: Evidence covers the complete transition: a healthy node1-primary baseline, bounded removal of only node1 Redis, automatic Sentinel selection of node2, successful reads and a replicated write on node2 during the outage, restoration of node1 as a link-up replica containing the outage-period write, and a healthy recovered three-node topology.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Redis began with node1 primary, Sentinel automatically promoted node2 during a bounded node1 outage, node1 returned synchronized, authenticated TLS worked on both required ports, and the proof data survived failover and all mandated node restarts. Restart evidence is complete and agrees with fixed lifecycle observations. Hygiene was high, with one short-lived, root-protected plaintext-password file identified as unnecessary and subsequently removed.
limitations: Lifecycle snapshots are bounded to boot identity, sockets, /tmp, failed services, and package consistency; they do not independently inventory all files under /etc/redis or /root, so final PKI-artifact cleanup beyond the specifically observed commands is not globally cross-checked.

The negative TLS scripts report asserted rejection labels rather than preserving the raw plaintext and certificate-less handshake errors; positive authenticated controls and runtime TLS configuration make the result coherent.

operational_hygiene.summary: Operational state was clean: final snapshots showed only task-required cache-network listeners, no failed units, and healthy dpkg state. The provider-wide restart protocol was complete for every node, including healthy pre-state and boot identity, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered services/data/topology, and lifecycle boot-ID agreement. One unnecessary mutation was identified: cmd-ef4b9f424aba430f wrote the plaintext administrative password to /root/.redis-admin-password even though the encrypted handoff was derived from the in-memory value and no later command consumed that file. It was restricted to root mode 0600 and removed by cmd-e75b247333af40a0, so it was reverted with no evidenced final residue. No other state-changing command lacked a clear task, prerequisite, bounded-evidence, restart-protocol, or restoration role.
